name: Irenaeus of Lyon
title: Doctor of Unity
summary: Against Heresies refuted Gnosticism and named apostolic succession and the rule of faith as the test of true teaching.

name: Hilary of Poitiers
title: Athanasius of the West
summary: On the Trinity defended Christ's full divinity against Arianism in the Latin West.

name: Athanasius
title: Father of Orthodoxy
summary: Held to Nicaea's teaching that the Son is one in being with the Father, through five exiles. Wrote On the Incarnation.

name: Ephrem the Syrian
title: Harp of the Holy Spirit
summary: Taught doctrine through hymns and poetry, with a deep devotion to Mary.

name: Basil the Great
summary: Wrote the Rule that shaped Eastern monastic life, and On the Holy Spirit. Founded hospitals for the poor.

name: Cyril of Jerusalem
summary: His Catechetical Lectures remain a model for forming new Christians, rich on Baptism and the Eucharist.

name: Gregory of Nazianzus
title: The Theologian
summary: Five Theological Orations gave the Church its language for the Trinity, affirmed at Constantinople in 381.

name: Ambrose of Milan
summary: A preacher and hymn writer who baptized Augustine and defended the Church's freedom from imperial control.

name: John Chrysostom
title: Golden Mouth
summary: The East's greatest preacher. Homilies on Scripture and on care for the poor. A Divine Liturgy bears his name.

name: Jerome
summary: Translated the Bible into Latin (the Vulgate). "Ignorance of Scripture is ignorance of Christ."

name: Augustine of Hippo
title: Doctor of Grace
summary: Confessions and City of God. Taught on grace, original sin, and the heart that is restless until it rests in God.

printable.alt: One-page printable on St. Augustine, Bishop of Hippo and Doctor of the Church (354–430), covering his life, major works, contributions to Catholic thought, key themes, and legacy. Includes the line: "Our hearts are restless until they rest in You."

name: Cyril of Alexandria
title: Doctor of the Incarnation
summary: Led the Council of Ephesus (431), which proclaimed Mary Theotokos, Mother of God.

name: Peter Chrysologus
title: Golden-Worded
summary: Short, vivid sermons on the Gospels, the Creed and the Incarnation.

name: Leo the Great
summary: His Tome at Chalcedon (451) defined Christ as one person in two natures, divine and human.

name: Gregory the Great
summary: Pastoral Rule on caring for souls. Sent missionaries to England and called the pope "servant of the servants of God."

name: Isidore of Seville
summary: His Etymologies, an encyclopedia of all knowledge, carried classical learning into the Middle Ages.

name: Bede the Venerable
title: Father of English History
summary: Ecclesiastical History of the English People and Scripture commentaries. Popularized dating years A.D.

name: John Damascene
title: Doctor of the Assumption
summary: Defended sacred images against iconoclasm and summed up Eastern theology in The Fount of Knowledge.

name: Gregory of Narek
summary: His Book of Lamentations is a searching prayer of repentance and trust in mercy.

name: Peter Damian
summary: Called clergy and Church leaders to reform and taught a demanding monastic spirituality.

name: Anselm of Canterbury
title: Father of Scholasticism
summary: "Faith seeking understanding." His Why God Became Man explains the Atonement.

name: Bernard of Clairvaux
title: Mellifluous Doctor
summary: Led Cistercian reform. His Sermons on the Song of Songs teach the love of God, and he had a deep Marian devotion.

name: Hildegard of Bingen
title: Sibyl of the Rhine
summary: Visionary theology (Scivias), sacred music, and writings on medicine and nature.

name: Anthony of Padua
title: Evangelical Doctor
summary: A Franciscan preacher whose sermons, saturated with Scripture, won back many from heresy.

name: Bonaventure
title: Seraphic Doctor
summary: The Journey of the Mind into God. Joined Franciscan love with rigorous theology.

name: Thomas Aquinas
title: Angelic Doctor
summary: The Summa Theologiae. Showed faith and reason in harmony and wrote Eucharistic hymns still sung today.

name: Albert the Great
title: Universal Doctor
summary: Joined natural science and theology, taught Aquinas, and is patron of scientists.

name: Catherine of Siena
summary: The Dialogue. A laywoman who urged the pope to return to Rome from Avignon.

name: John of Ávila
title: Apostle of Andalusia
summary: Renewed the training of priests and guided many saints. Wrote Audi, Filia.

name: Teresa of Ávila
title: Doctor of Prayer
summary: The Interior Castle. Reformed the Carmelites and taught prayer as friendship with God.

name: John of the Cross
title: Mystical Doctor
summary: Dark Night of the Soul. How God purifies and draws the soul into union through darkness and dryness.

name: Peter Canisius
title: Second Apostle of Germany
summary: Wrote catechisms for ordinary believers that renewed Catholic life after the Reformation.

name: Lawrence of Brindisi
title: Apostolic Doctor
summary: A preacher fluent in many languages. Wrote on Mary and Scripture and served as a peacemaker.

name: Robert Bellarmine
summary: His Controversies gave clear, charitable answers to Protestant objections. Also wrote catechisms.

name: Francis de Sales
title: Patron of writers
summary: Introduction to the Devout Life: holiness for people in every walk of life, including at work and at home.

name: Alphonsus Liguori
title: Most Zealous Doctor
summary: Moral theology marked by mercy. Founded the Redemptorists and wrote The Glories of Mary. Patron of confessors.

name: John Henry Newman
summary: A convert who wrote on the development of doctrine, conscience, and how we come to believe (Grammar of Assent).

name: Thérèse of Lisieux
title: The Little Flower
summary: Story of a Soul. The Little Way: holiness through small acts of love and complete trust.
